scope: Sanitized manager synthesis of current source-bound allocation-study artifacts and a complete paginated raw-turn audit. It does not accept an edition, measure translation benefit, or establish a Top 10.

accepted_rules: A population, country, macrolanguage, route, or catalogue row is not an exact edition identity.
Every natural edition binds exact variety, script or orthography, territory or educational standard, scholarly canon, stage, subject and delivery scope.
A faithful 722-unit OpenLogic edition and a bounded local-needs companion are separate artifacts with separate coverage manifests.
Semantic translation, regional adaptation, script projection, pronunciation accessibility and notation profile are distinct typed layers.

OpenLogic and forall x principally support proof and research access; secondary use requires explicit prerequisites, while foundational or early-literacy packages are separately authored and receive no OpenLogic coverage credit.
Interlanguage benefit is unmeasured in the selected evidence; shared-register editions remain labelled experiments and do not replace native editions.
Reference retrieval, definition learning, proof comprehension and worked-example transfer are separate evaluation endpoints.
Accessibility is a separate marginal-access axis and bounded accessibility does not equal complete accessibility.
Source length, census language groups, PISA burdens, catalogue counts and stage tags do not determine language priority, effect or rank.
publication_baselines: low-bitrate media variants when media exist

specific_guards.Arabic: The current formal MSA edition does not establish vernacular or oral-route coverage; digit variants are notation profiles.
specific_guards.Persian: Iranian Persian, Dari and Tajik are separate natural/curriculum targets; Inter-Farsi is additional experimental infrastructure.
specific_guards.Hindi_Urdu: A shared technical profile is experimental; Urdu is not a transliterated Hindi edition.
specific_guards.Punjabi: Pakistan Shahmukhi and Indian Gurmukhi require separate natural-edition evidence; Naskh and Nastaliq can remain typography profiles over one Shahmukhi text.
specific_guards.Pashto: A broad PUSHTO or displacement row cannot be assigned to one Pakistan or Afghanistan variety.
specific_guards.Bengali: India and Bangladesh standards remain separate targets even where terminology is shared.
specific_guards.Indonesian: Official Grade VII supply means Indonesia is neither a blank-textbook case nor solved; Malay and local-language routes remain separate.
specific_guards.Interslavic: Do not claim family coverage; rebalance the Russian/Ukrainian-heavy basis before a new release and evaluate four mathematical task types separately.

not_actionable: Any current Top 10 or Top 100 claim
A route or population row as proof that a translation exists
Interlanguage cost thresholds as measured comprehension or compute
PISA, census, token or catalogue values as edition benefit
A mechanically possible script conversion without a readership case and script-aware QA
A raw-turn assertion of Indonesian 722/722 completion without independent anonymous release and closure verification
